title: Pasta with Anchovies and Toasted Breadcrumbs
subtitle: Sardinian-style spaghetti with anchovy, garlic, and crisp crumbs
excerpt: A simple southern Italian pasta where anchovies melt into the oil and toasted breadcrumbs take the place of cheese. Fast, punchy, and surprisingly light.
sourceNotes: Based on the Sicilian and Sardinian tradition of pasta con le acciughe e mollica, a peasant dish that uses breadcrumbs instead of parmesan.

content.text: Toast the breadcrumbs in a separate dry pan so you can control the colour without worrying about the pasta.

items.prepNote: 2 for the breadcrumbs, 3 for the anchovy oil
2 tbsp for breadcrumbs, 4 tbsp for anchovy sauce

content.text: Cook the spaghetti in a large pan of well-salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve a mug of pasta water before draining.
While the pasta cooks, heat 2 tbsp olive oil in the frying pan. Add 2 sliced garlic cloves and the breadcrumbs.
Toast over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring constantly, until golden and crisp. Season with salt. Tip into a bowl and set aside.
Wipe the pan. Heat the remaining 4 tbsp olive oil over medium-low heat. Add the 3 remaining crushed garlic cloves and the chilli flakes.
Add the anchovy fillets. Stir for 2 minutes until they dissolve into the oil.
Add the drained spaghetti to the pan. Toss over low heat, adding a splash of pasta water to loosen.
Add the parsley and lemon zest. Toss again.
Serve in bowls topped with the toasted breadcrumbs.

items.cause: Not enough pasta water added when tossing.
items.fix: Add the reserved pasta water 2 tbsp at a time until the pasta moves freely.

items.cause: Added too early or pasta was too wet.
items.fix: Add breadcrumbs at the table so each person can scatter their own.
